ph: With the President of Kenya, Hon. Daniel Arap Moi at the State House, 26 Aug 99

w: Shri Pramod Mahajan - Central Minister for Information and Technology, Shri Dr Kurien - former chairman of National Dairy Development Board and H.E. Sundersinh Bhandari - the Governor of Gujarat arrived for the opening of 'Pramukh Swami Computer Institute' (PCI). Swamishri welcomed them with garlands. The PCI is in affiliation with Louisiana State University, USA.

Swamishri was asked to write a message for a space mission called SIRTF MISSION (Space Infrared Telescope Facility), that will travel around the Sun to study it and other stars. All those associated with the making and planning of the mission have been asked to write their own signature or poetry or make a sketch.

Shri Jitu Mehta, a devotee, who contributed as a flight software development manager, believed that he was able to accomplish the work through Swamishri's blessings. So he asked Swamishri to write a message. In response, Swamishri wrote in Gujarati, "Atma Paramatmanu yatharth gnan thaay tyare aa lokni bhautik icchaao vasanaao tali jaay ne Bhagwan nu Akshardhamna sukhne pami sukhiyo thaay."

Swamishri's message is, "When man absolutely realizes the knowledge of atma and Paramatma, then his material desires of this world are dissolved and he becomes happy by attaining the bliss of God's Akshardham (abode)."
The essence of all of Swamishri's discourses or messages, no matter what the occasion or function be, pivots around realizing the knowledge of atma and Paramatma for eternal happiness.
Swamishri came to know of a volunteer's habit and love for eating out. On seeing him, Swamishri reproached, "Do you ever think of eating poison?"
Chandrakant, the volunteer, humorously said, "By eating out I feel healthy, whereas by eating at home I get sick."
Swamishri responded seriously, "You are mad. Yesterday (in the drama) the boy was brave and resolute in not eating out, whereas you allow for such lapses!"
A sadhu added, "He believes that there's nothing wrong in eating out. Does it stop one from being a satsangi?"
Swamishri replied authoritatively, "Yes, it stops one from being a satsangi!"
Then Swamishri pulling a volunteer's scarf standing near him asked, "You go about wearing this scarf but what are you doing?"
The volunteer said, "I don't eat out!"
Swamishri said, "I'm referring in general. A volunteer should not have lapses. One must be staunch in one's moral conduct."
Then Swamishri told a senior volunteer, "Enquire of him now and then and write a report to me. If you come to know that he eats out then fine him accordingly."

Swamishri's emphasis for all devotees not to eat out is apparent by his strong dislike for it. He often stresses that eating out is not healthy for the body, mind and soul. This kusang contaminates one's mind and personal spirituality.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
17 Aug 2002, Amdavad
Swamishri showered flowers on 70 devotees who had pilgrimaged on foot from Ghodasar to the Swaminarayan Mandir in Shahibaug (11 km).
376 kishores and 350 kishoris had pilgrimaged on foot from various suburbs of Amdavad to the mandir on Kishore Day.
2 kishores performed 2,500 prostrations from their home to the mandir on Kishore Day.
For the last 3 years, each member of the Amdavad Kishore Mandal has been fasting a day for Swamishri's good health.
18 August 2002, Amdavad
On the occasion of Children's Day program, a satsangi child, Akshar, performed 2,500 prostrations from Gomtipur to the mandir. Swamishri blessed the boy.
21 August 2002, Amdavad
Swamishri blessed 200 devotees who had performed austerities like chandrayan, dharna-parna, khatras, etc.
22 August 2002, Amdavad
About 300 devotees from Gandhinagar had pilgrimaged on foot to Amdavad (26 km) out of which 7 kishores had performed 1965 prostrations.
Twenty-two disabled boys and girls had pilgrimaged on foot from Uvaarsad (29 km).
Eighteen kishores had performed prostrations from Sabarmati to the mandir in Shahibaug (7.5 km), beginning at 12.30 a.m.
25 August 2002, Amdavad
Two-and-a-half-year-old Kush Patel pilgrimaged by foot from Nava Vadaj to the mandir (6 km).

Day 2 - National Kishore-Kishori Summer Shibir The final day of the Kishore-Kishori Shibir saw Swamishri performing puja surrounded by the murtis of Nilkanth Varni - The Ideal Kishore. Swamishri sanctified all the murtis with flowers. During the day, senior sadhus and kishore co-ordinators presented the principles of Swaminarayan Sanskruti.

The evening commenced with a kirtan bhakti performance by sadhus, which led onto an inspiring programme presented by kishores on Shastriji Maharaj and his greatest gift to us - Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Swamishri was welcomed by a colourful dance and was seated on a glorious stage with the Sarangpur gate, mandir and Smruti Mandir as a backdrop. Swamishri blessed the assembly and explained the importance of the Akshar Purushottam philosophy and how Shastriji Maharaj had toiled day and night to establish this true philosophy. Swamishri then sprayed Thakorji with saffron-coloured water, following which all the kishores were sprayed by Swamishri as part of the joyous festival of Fuldol.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for the BAPS hari mandir in Dudhvada.

Brahmavihari Swami said, "The travelling you have done is beyond anyone's imagination, even in a dream. Because of the travelling you have done, no one else can afford to be lazy. In this organisation no one else can sit around lazily. And not only that, you have made wonderful efforts to keep everyone, young and old, happy. You have done padharamanis at the same devotee's home five times over."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj went ten times over. They went as many times as they were asked."
Krishnavallabh Swami said, "But in those days they had to search for devotees!"
Swamishri said, "They laid the foundation, and we are building on top of it. Otherwise, what have we done?"
Brahmavihari Swami said, "But to keep everyone happy, you have gone to their homes even when there was no occasion there. Why go just like that, without any occasion?"
Swamishri said, "What is lost by it?"
Brahmavihari Swami said, "But there is hardship!"

Swamishri said, "The hardship is to the body. How is there any hardship to the atma? If we think of the body, nothing gets done, not even seva. That is not to be done at all! Do not look at the body at all."
After hearing these words from Swamishri at the age of 90, who would feel like sitting idle?
After reading letters, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was getting up to go and rest. Dr Nikul was measuring his blood pressure. He said, "Leader at 90."
"What is that?" Swamishri asked.

Brahmavihari Swami said, "I gave a talk abroad on how you are leading the organisation even at the age of 90. Its essence was that the universe of BAPS is now contained in one wheelchair, and that wheelchair has today spread across the whole universe."
Swamishri said, "Meaning?"
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Sitting in a wheelchair, you are running the whole vast organisation."
Swamishri said, "We do not do anything. Maharaj does everything."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Just as Maharaj does everything while sitting in Akshardham...."

Stopping him midway, Swamishri pointed his finger upwards and said, "Because he is sitting up there, everything happens here. It is only Shriji Maharaj's power that works. It is his wish and his work. Everything goes on through the grace of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogi Bapa. Nothing goes on through us. It is his power, his wish, his work, all of this...." Having said this, Swamishri got up to go and rest.

Today a new murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni was to be installed in the abhishek mandap here. When Mahant Swami Maharaj set out from his residence for this, the devotees began loudly calling out, "Mahant Swami Maharaj ni jai... Mahant Swami Maharaj ni jai..." Hearing this, Swamishri stopped. His face fell. He said, "Always call out 'Pramukh Swami Maharaj ni jai' first."
The devotees at once accepted this command and called out a sky splitting jai for Pramukh Swami Maharaj. In that cry everyone heard the echoes of Swamishri's devotion to his guru.

Today, on the occasion of the tribute assembly for Pramukh Swami Maharaj, artistic garlands had come to welcome Mahant Swami Maharaj. While putting them on him, the sadhus were also making beautiful prayers. In this series one sadhu said, "When a new king comes, he forgives crimes; in the same way, please forgive our crimes too."
"The old ones are forgiven, but do not commit new ones..." Swamishri said graciously.

What power of the Satpurush, to burn to ashes in a single moment the heaps of sins of countless births! Here the lines "In the refuge of such a great one, the sins of past births are burnt..." are always fulfilled.
In today's shibir session, a series of questions and answers with Mahant Swami Maharaj began.
Question: "How did you get the inspiration to become a sadhu?"

Swamishri said, "Pramukh Swami Maharaj was going to Ahmedabad on an ekadashi day, and I was in the same train compartment. I knew him, but it was there that I came to know him closely. He spoke to me about renunciation and detachment, that this worldly life is not worth falling into, and so on. He also spoke about keeping the ekadashi fast. So the first inspiration was given by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Then Yogi Bapa followed it up."
Question: "Have you ever been troubled in life?"
Swamishri said, "There is trouble, but not that kind. Sattvik trouble. Even such trouble came once or twice, not every day."
The question was asked, "Have you ever been troubled about yourself?"
"No." Then, waving his hand, he said, "Once I met Bapa, there was nothing." That is, there had never been any such trouble.
Question: "How should we understand that you and Pramukh Swami Maharaj are one?"

"Through understanding, through knowledge." Then he said, "Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj all seem different outwardly, but in their form they are all one. But they come in the line, not going beyond Pramukh Swami Maharaj."
Question: "It takes time to gain knowledge, and we expect experience. Is that right?"

Swamishri said, "Shastriji Maharaj said, 'The great sadhu never leaves the earth.' That covers millions of years. Gunatitanand Swami said, 'He will remain for at least ten or twenty generations.' And we hear the proof of this from the scriptures and from the lips of the manifest guru. Yogi Bapa also said, 'The great sadhu will remain in the future too.' We have to have faith in this. And why would there not be faith? We have such a guru. And what reason is there to lie about it?! One cannot lie in such matters, or there would be great confusion. We have to work with faith; then the experience comes."
Immediately the question was asked, "If you gave us the experience first, wouldn't it be less of a struggle?"
"No, it happens only in order," Swamishri said.
